newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end up, market picks up confidence.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end up, market picks up confidence.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Thursday after a strong upward move in U.S. Treasuries on the back of tame economic indicator releases.
Traders said after the recent sessions spent worrying about U.S. rates and inflation, the scene now looked set for the market to be able to stabilize.
"The worst has passed," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 3/8 at 74-3/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 rose $0.20 to 120.15.
With the U.S. Treasury market feeling less worried about the inflation outlook, Argentine bonds were likely to reduce their spreads to U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
"Clearly, the favorable market conditions have not changed at all. The outlook is for gradually smaller spreads," said another trader.
The market paid little attention to Thursday's strike staged by the CTA and MTA opposition unions, traders said.
In the money market, one week peso BAIBOR, or Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, rose to 7.1875 percent from 7.0625 percent.
